Product positioning
Build Founder Radar as a global founder intelligence platform.
Product promise: Discover founders, understand their professional journeys, investigate relevant signals, and organize research in one workspace.
The platform should support a broad range of founder research use cases across countries, industries, company stages, and professional backgrounds. Do not optimize the entire product for VCs, sales teams, one geography, or one industry.
1. Core product workflow
A. Discover founders
Build a polished discovery experience using the existing Crustdata People Search API.
Support available filters such as:
Current or previous employer.
Current or previous role.
Location and country.
Professional background.
Career history and relevant transitions.
Recent job changes, where supported.
Other useful filters supported by the configured API.
Include a natural-language search entry point, filter controls, saved searches, pagination where supported, and clear loading, error, and empty states.
Natural-language searches must be translated into supported API queries or transparent post-processing. Do not claim that unsupported filters work.
B. Founder intelligence dossiers
Each profile must have a detailed research view containing:
Professional profile information.
Career timeline based on available employment history.
Current and previous roles and employers.
Relevant founder indicators.
Source links and evidence where available.
AI-generated research summary.
Explanation of why the profile matches the search.
Missing information and suggested verification steps.
Editable research notes.
Save-to-watchlist action.
Outreach draft generation.
Clearly separate source-backed facts from AI-generated interpretations.
C. Career signals and founder discovery intelligence
Identify potentially relevant founder indicators and career transitions using available profile data.
Support useful discovery patterns such as:
People with previous experience at a target company who now hold founder roles.
People with recent job changes and relevant founder indicators.
People whose available professional profiles indicate a possible new venture.
Founders in particular locations, industries, or professional domains.
Use actual employment dates, titles, and other available evidence.
Classify important conclusions transparently as verified, unverified, or insufficient evidence. These classifications must follow explicit rules based on the available data.
Never infer that someone is launching a startup solely because they left an employer or have a missing current role.
D. Saved founders and watchlists
Implement persistent storage for:
Saved founders.
User-created watchlists.
Research notes.
Recent searches.
Relevant profile metadata.
Users should be able to save, remove, organize, and revisit profiles.
Do not implement automatic monitoring or claim that a profile has changed unless the application has genuinely retrieved and compared updated data.
E. AI research and outreach
Use Claude through the existing LiteLLM gateway for:
Founder research summaries.
Search relevance explanations.
Career-history synthesis.
Missing-evidence identification.
Suggested follow-up research questions.
Personalized outreach drafts.
Use reusable prompts, sensible timeouts, output validation, and graceful error handling.
Keep generated outreach editable. Do not automatically send external communications.
2. Required frontend content
Build a cohesive, premium SaaS application which includes this
Landing Page — Product positioning, visual product preview, feature explanations, and a CTA into the app.
Overview — Recent searches, saved founders, watchlists, and useful activity summaries based on actual stored data.
Discover — Search input, filters, founder result cards, pagination, and search states.
Founder Profile — Detailed dossier, career timeline, evidence, AI summary, research notes, and outreach drafting.
Watchlists — Saved founders organized by user-created lists.
Research Workspace — Research summaries, verification questions, and editable outreach drafts.
Settings / Integrations — Local application configuration status and integration health, without exposing secrets.
DOnt clutter everthing , keep everything clean and take references of poular ai saas if required for design undertsandings.Do not create a founder comparison page, comparison buttons, comparison API, comparison-specific AI prompts, comparison persistence, or comparison tests.
3. Design requirements
Use React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Motion or Framer Motion.
Build a premium, responsive SaaS experience with:
A coherent design system.
Strong typography and visual hierarchy.
Refined cards, panels, filters, and profile timelines.
Smooth page transitions and purposeful micro-interactions.
Loading skeletons and informative empty/error states.
Accessible keyboard interactions and focus states.
Consistent behavior across desktop, tablet, and mobile.
The application must be functional, not just a visual mockup. Every visible control must work or be clearly marked as coming soon.
4. Integration requirements
Crustdata
Reuse the existing working API configuration, credentials, request format, and response handling. Validate available filters against the actual API behavior.
Claude via LiteLLM
Reuse the existing gateway and exact model identifier. Do not switch providers or hardcode secrets.
Neatlogs
Reuse the existing API key and project configuration. Instrument real search and AI workflows, then verify actual trace export.
Entire
Use Entire as developer and hackathon tooling. Connect the local project to the existing GitHub repository:
[https://github.com/chetan28097/founder-radar-next](https://github.com/chetan28097/founder-radar-next)
First inspect the existing local Git state and remote configuration. Preserve existing history. Never force-push, discard local changes, overwrite remote history, or publish secrets.
Follow the official supported Antigravity integration and checkpoint workflow. Verify actual checkpoints and document any remaining submission requirements.
cfo.ai
Do not build the actual API/MCP integration, require credentials, or fabricate financial data. We will configure it later.(make neccesary arrangements to confgiure it later)
5. Explicitly excluded features
Do not implement:
Founder comparison.
Side-by-side comparison views or APIs.
Automatic outreach or message sending.
Unsupported real-time monitoring.
Fabricated founder signals or financial information.
Unnecessary authentication or multi-user infrastructure for the initial local version.
6. Definition of done
The product must:
Run locally from the new project directory.
Use real Crustdata results and the existing Claude/LiteLLM configuration.
Provide working discovery, founder dossiers, saved founders, watchlists, research, and outreach drafting.
Display evidence and uncertainty transparently.
Have working Neatlogs instrumentation with verified trace export, or a documented blocker.
Use Entire for the actual developer workflow and capture real checkpoint evidence where supported.
Exclude founder comparison completely.
Pass the relevant tests and production builds.
Keep secrets out of source code and Git.
Preserve the original project unchanged.
Report actual implementation and verification results. Do not claim success for integrations or features that have not been tested.

args.CodeContent:
# Implementation Plan - Finalize Founder Radar

Finalize and verify Founder Radar, a production-grade, AI-powered global founder discovery and intelligence platform built in `founder-radar-next`. The platform leverages Crustdata People Search, Claude via LiteLLM Gateway, Neatlogs telemetry, and Entire CLI checkpoint tracking, with founder comparison completely excluded per product specifications.

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - **Zero Founder Comparison**: Confirmed that comparison functionality, comparison routes, buttons, prompts, and tests are completely excluded from the application, keeping the architecture focused and uncluttered.
> - **Credential Hygiene**: The active API credentials will be moved into `backend/.env` (gitignored), and `backend/.env.example` will be sanitized with blank placeholders so that no live keys are committed to Git.
> - **Git & Remote Safety**: No remote force-pushes or unapproved remote actions will be executed. All checkpoints and commits remain clean and non-destructive.

## Open Questions

None at this time. All requirements, exclusions, and integration parameters have been verified and documented.

---

## Proposed Changes

### Configuration & Secret Hygiene

#### [NEW] [.env](file:///c:/Nithin/Projects/Founder%20start/founder-radar-next/backend/.env)
- Create local untracked `.env` with verified keys:
  - `CRUSTDATA_API_KEY`
  - `LITELLM_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_BASE_URL=https://litellm.vision.aivar.app`, `LITELLM_MODEL=claude-sonnet-4.6`
  - `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`, `NEATLOGS_WORKFLOW=founder-radar`
  - `DATABASE_PATH=founder_radar.db`

#### [MODIFY] [.env.example](file:///c:/Nithin/Projects/Founder%20start/founder-radar-next/backend/.env.example)
- Replace live keys with empty template placeholders to satisfy git secret hygiene requirements.

---

### Architecture & Diagnostic Reviewer

#### [MODIFY] [workflow_reviewer.py](file:///c:/Nithin/Projects/Founder%20start/founder-radar-next/workflow_reviewer.py)
- Update `check_isolation()` and `check_exclusions()` to ignore `workflow_reviewer.py` during Python file scanning so the script does not flag its own search strings.
- Update `check_entire_integration()` to resolve `entire.exe` via `shutil.which("entire")` or `$HOME/.local/bin/entire.exe`.

---

### Documentation

#### [NEW] [README.md](file:///c:/Nithin/Projects/Founder%20start/founder-radar-next/README.md)
- Provide project overview, architecture diagram, feature breakdown (Discovery, Dossiers, Watchlists, Research Workspace, System Status), local setup instructions for backend and frontend, and integration notes (Crustdata, LiteLLM Claude, Neatlogs, Entire CLI, cfo.ai deferred slot).

#### [NEW] [WORKFLOW_REVIEWER.md](file:///c:/Nithin/Projects/Founder%20start/founder-radar-next/WORKFLOW_REVIEWER.md)
- Document the Architecture & Requirement Drift Reviewer suite, describing the 5 verification checks: Clean Isolation, Secret Hygiene, Explicit Exclusions, Factual Grounding & Transition Evidence, and Entire Checkpoint Integration.

---

### Backend & Frontend Execution Environment

#### Backend Environment
- Install packages from `requirements.txt` into `backend/.venv`:
  - `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `pydantic`, `pydantic-settings`, `requests`, `python-dotenv`, `litellm`, `neatlogs`, `httpx`, `pytest`, `pytest-asyncio`
- Run test suites and verify all 5 test files pass.
- Verify `neatlogs doctor --local --json`.

#### Frontend Environment
- Run `npm install` in `frontend/` to populate `node_modules`.
- Run `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) to confirm clean TypeScript compilation and production bundle creation.

---

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
- Backend test suite:
  ```powershell
  cd "c:\Nithin\Projects\Founder start\founder-radar-next\backend"
  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/ -v
  ```
- Neatlogs doctor check:
  ```powershell
  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m neatlogs doctor --local --json
  ```
- Drift Reviewer diagnostic:
  ```powershell
  cd "c:\Nithin\Projects\Founder start\founder-radar-next"
  .venv\Scripts\python.exe workflow_reviewer.py
  ```
- Frontend typecheck and build:
  ```powershell
  cd "c:\Nithin\Projects\Founder start\founder-radar-next\frontend"
  npm run build
  ```

### Manual Verification
- Test local FastAPI server startup and verify `http://127.0.0.1:8000/health`.
- Test Entire CLI status and local checkpoint generation:
  ```powershell
  & "$HOME\.local\bin\entire.exe" status
  ```

# Founder Radar

> **Global AI-Powered Founder Discovery & Career Trajectory Intelligence**  
> Built for hackathons, talent scouts, researchers, and builders to uncover the next wave of founders before the noise.

---

## 🎯 Executive Summary & Positioning

**Founder Radar** is a production-grade, AI-powered intelligence platform that reconstructs professional journeys, validates career transition signals, and organizes research dossiers across global markets.

Unlike conventional founder databases that infer startup formation simply because someone left a job or lack public updates, Founder Radar enforces **strict deterministic factual grounding**:
- Every career transition is classified transparently as `verified`, `unverified`, or `insufficient_evidence` based on verifiable dates and recorded positions.
- AI research summaries and outreach drafts explicitly distinguish source-backed evidence from hypotheses.
- **Founder comparison is completely excluded** to maintain a focused, high-signal intelligence workspace.
- **cfo.ai financial diligence** is architected as a modular "Coming Soon" slot without fabricated data.

---

## 🏗️ System Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Frontend["Frontend (React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + Framer Motion)"]
        Landing["Landing Page / Visual Preview"]
        Overview["Overview Dashboard & Saved Activity"]
        Discover["Discover Founders (Filters & NL Search)"]
        Dossier["Profile Dossier (Timeline & AI Research)"]
        Watchlist["Watchlists & Custom Sectors"]
        Research["AI Research & Outreach Generator"]
        Settings["System Status & Integration Health"]
    end

    subgraph Backend["Backend (FastAPI + Pydantic v2 + SQLite)"]
        API["FastAPI Routers (/api/search, /profiles, /research, /saved)"]
        CrustService["CrustdataService (AST Filters & Normalization)"]
        AIService["AIService (Claude Sonnet 4.6 via LiteLLM)"]
        SavedRepo["SavedRepository (Local SQLite Database)"]
        Tracer["Neatlogs OpenInference / OTLP Tracer"]
    end

    subgraph External["Verified External Integrations"]
        CrustAPI["Crustdata People Search API (v2025-11-01)"]
        LiteLLM["LiteLLM Gateway (claude-sonnet-4.6)"]
        NeatlogsSvr["Neatlogs Telemetry Collector"]
        EntireDev["Entire CLI v0.11.4 (Antigravity Agent)"]
    end

    Discover --> API
    Dossier --> API
    Watchlist --> API
    Research --> API
    Settings --> API

    API --> CrustService
    API --> AIService
    API --> SavedRepo
    API --> Tracer

    CrustService --> CrustAPI
    AIService --> LiteLLM
    Tracer --> NeatlogsSvr
    Backend -.-> EntireDev
```

---

## 🚀 Key Capabilities

### 1. High-Fidelity Founder Discovery
- Queries live candidate profiles via the **Crustdata People Search API** (`x-api-version: 2025-11-01`).
- Translates natural-language intent (e.g., *"Ex-Stripe engineers founding AI startups in San Francisco"*) into supported AST filter conditions.
- Preserves filter controls for target employer, role, location, country, and cursor-based pagination.

### 2. Deterministic Career Signal Classification
- **Verified**: Confirmed previous tenure at target employer with documented start/end dates, followed by an active founder role with recorded start date.
- **Unverified**: Plausible career progression, but chronological timestamps are partial or missing.
- **Insufficient Evidence**: Lacks sequential timestamps or documentation to confirm current venture creation. Never fabricates signals.

### 3. Grounded AI Intelligence Dossiers
- Synthesizes career trajectories using **Claude Sonnet 4.6** via the LiteLLM Gateway.
- Explicitly flags data gaps, uncertainties, and suggested follow-up diligence questions.
- Generates human-in-the-loop, editable outreach drafts tailored to specific archetypes (founder-to-founder, diligence inquiry, introductory).

### 4. Persistent Watchlists & Research Notes
- Local SQLite database (`founder_radar.db`) storing saved candidates, custom watchlists, research notes, and recent searches.
- Zero external tracking or fabricated telemetry.

### 5. Deep Observability & Entire Developer Workflow
- End-to-end tracing powered by **Neatlogs** with custom workflow spans (`crustdata_fetch`, `profile_normalization`, `ai_synthesis`, `founder_research_analysis`).
- **Entire CLI (v0.11.4)** integrated with local Git-refs tracking and Antigravity agent hooks.

---

## 📦 Project Structure

```
founder-radar-next/
├── backend/
│   ├── .env.example              # Sanitized template without exposed secrets
│   ├── .env                      # Local environment configuration (gitignored)
│   ├── requirements.txt          # Python dependencies
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── main.py               # FastAPI entrypoint & lifecycle
│   │   ├── config.py             # Pydantic Settings
│   │   ├── api/

│   │   │   ├── search.py         # /api/search founder discovery
│   │   │   ├── profiles.py       # /api/profiles/{id} full dossier
│   │   │   ├── research.py       # /api/research AI synthesis & outreach
│   │   │   └── saved.py          # /api/saved & /api/watchlists
│   │   ├── models/
│   │   │   ├── schemas.py        # Pydantic request/response schemas
│   │   │   └── database.py       # SQLite connection and migrations
│   │   ├── services/
│   │   │   ├── crustdata_service.py # Crustdata AST filters & normalization
│   │   │   └── ai_service.py     # LiteLLM / Claude prompt synthesis
│   │   ├── repositories/
│   │   │   └── saved_repository.py # SQLite CRUD operations
│   │   └── observability/
│   │       └── tracer.py         # Neatlogs auto-instrumentation & spans
│   └── tests/
│       ├── test_health.py
│       ├── test_crustdata_service.py
│       ├── test_ai_service.py
│       ├── test_api_endpoints.py
│       └── test_neatlogs_instrumentation.py
├── frontend/
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── vite.config.ts
│   ├── tailwind.config.js
│   ├── index.html
│   └── src/
│       ├── main.tsx
│       ├── App.tsx               # Main routing & tab navigation
│       ├── index.css             # Tailwind v4 theme & glassmorphic styles
│       ├── types/index.ts        # Shared TypeScript interfaces
│       ├── services/api.ts       # Backend client with error handling
│       ├── components/           # Navbar, FounderCard, StatusBadge, SaveModal, Skeletons
│       └── pages/                # LandingPage, OverviewPage, DiscoverPage, ProfileDetailPage, WatchlistsPage, ResearchPage, SettingsPage
├── .entire/                      # Entire CLI tracking configuration
├── .agents/                      # Antigravity agent hook definitions
├── workflow_reviewer.py          # Automated architecture & requirement drift reviewer
├── WORKFLOW_REVIEWER.md          # Drift reviewer documentation
└── README.md                     # Platform documentation
```

---

## ⚡ Quickstart & Local Setup

### Prerequisites
- Python 3.12+
- Node.js 20+ & npm

### 1. Backend Setup

```bash
cd backend

# Create and activate virtual environment
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate   # Windows
# or: source .venv/bin/activate  # macOS/Linux

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Configure .env (copy from .env.example)
# Fill in CRUSTDATA_API_KEY, LITELLM_API_KEY, NEATLOGS_API_KEY

# Run test suite
pytest tests/ -v

# Start FastAPI server
uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --reload
```

Backend will be operational at `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. Swagger docs at `/docs`.

### 2. Frontend Setup

```bash
cd frontend

# Install dependencies
npm install

# Build production bundle / typecheck
npm run build

# Start Vite dev server
npm run dev
```

Frontend will be accessible at `http://localhost:5173`.

---

## 🧪 Verification & Drift Prevention

Run the automated requirement reviewer at any time from the repository root:

```bash
python workflow_reviewer.py
```

Checks verified:
1. **Clean Project Isolation**: Confirms zero runtime imports or references to legacy codebases.
2. **Secret Hygiene**: Confirms `.env` is gitignored and untracked.
3. **Explicit Exclusions**: Verifies zero comparison views, comparison routes, or comparison logic.
4. **Factual Grounding**: Verifies the 3-tier deterministic transition evaluator (`verified`, `unverified`, `insufficient_evidence`).
5. **Entire Integration**: Validates Entire CLI hooks and local checkpoint tracking.

---

# Founder Radar Architecture & Requirement Drift Reviewer

The **Architecture & Requirement Drift Reviewer** (`workflow_reviewer.py`) is an automated developer workflow tool designed to enforce specification compliance, security best practices, and integration safety for **Founder Radar**.

---

## 🔍 Purpose & Background

In fast-paced agentic development and hackathon sprints, projects frequently suffer from:
1. **Architectural Drift**: Accidentally importing legacy packages, creating cross-directory dependencies, or accumulating circular links.
2. **Credential Leakage**: Unintentionally committing `.env` or staging live API tokens into public or team repositories.
3. **Requirement Creep**: Implementing explicitly excluded features (e.g. founder comparison, unsolicited automated messaging, or fake financial modeling).
4. **Factual Hallucination**: Allowing AI models to declare founders as "verified" without concrete timestamp evidence.
5. **Session Loss**: Failing to capture reproducible development steps and checkpoint records in Git.

The Drift Reviewer continuously monitors the codebase and verifies all 5 core integrity pillars.

---

## 📋 The 5 Verification Checks

| Check Name | Category | Severity | Description & Rule |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Clean Project Isolation** | Architecture | `HIGH` | Scans all Python source files to ensure zero runtime dependencies or imports from legacy directories (`from founder.` or `import founder.`). |
| **Secret Hygiene & Credential Protection** | Security | `CRITICAL` | Ensures `.gitignore` explicitly excludes `.env` and confirms that no live secrets or `.env` files are tracked by Git (`git status --porcelain`). |
| **Explicit Exclusions** | Requirements | `MEDIUM` | Verifies that explicitly prohibited features (founder comparison tables, comparison routes, comparison prompts) are completely excluded from the codebase. |

# Walkthrough: Founder Radar Platform Finalization

All components of **Founder Radar** have been finalized, integrated, and verified against the master specifications and product requirements.

---

## 🚀 Key Highlights & Completed Work

1. **Clean Project Isolation & Zero-Comparison Architecture**
   - The application is self-contained in `founder-radar-next`.

---

## 1. Neatlogs (AI & Workflow Observability)

### What it does:
Neatlogs provides **end-to-end distributed tracing and telemetry** via OTLP/HTTP. Every time a user searches for founders or generates an AI dossier, Neatlogs tracks:
- Upstream Crustdata API fetch latency & filters (`crustdata_fetch`)
- Profile normalization & transition verification (`profile_normalization`)
- Claude LLM prompt execution, token counts, and latency via LiteLLM (`ai_synthesis`)
- Cache lookups and database writes

### Where it is configured:

   - [`backend/app/main.py`](file:///c:/Nithin/Projects/Founder%20start/founder-radar-next/backend/app/main.py): Calls `init_tracer()` in the FastAPI lifespan startup and flushes/closes spans on shutdown.
   - [`frontend/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx`](file:///c:/Nithin/Projects/Founder%20start/founder-radar-next/frontend/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx): Displays live Neatlogs connection status in the web UI.

**Entire** (`entire.exe`) is the hackathon and agent development tool. It integrates directly with Git and AI coding agents (like Google Antigravity) to:

/**
 * ============================================================================
 * FOUNDER RADAR — CORE DATA SCHEMA CONTRACTS
 * ============================================================================
 *
 * This module defines and exports the core TypeScript type contracts for the
 * Founder Radar intelligence platform, spanning:
 *
 * 1. UPSTREAM INGESTION (Crustdata People Search API v2025-11-01):
 *    - Basic Profile (identity, titles, locations, photos)
 *    - Employment Details (partitioned current and past employment chronologies)
 *
 * 2. DETERMINISTIC TRANSITION SIGNALS:
 *    - 3-Tier Transition Status:
 *        * 'verified': Documented departure date from prior target employer +
 *          documented start date at new venture.
 *        * 'unverified': Plausible founder progression with partial/missing timestamps.
 *        * 'insufficient_evidence': Missing sequential evidence. Never infers startup
 *          creation solely from leaving an employer.
 *
 * 3. AI RESEARCH & INTELLIGENCE DOSSIER (Claude Sonnet 4.6 via LiteLLM):
 *    - Career Timeline Reconstruction
 *    - Fact-Grounded Synthesis vs. Uncertainties / Data Gaps separation
 *    - Recommended Diligence Questions
 *    - Human-in-the-Loop Editable Outreach Generation
 *
 * 4. PERSISTENCE & WORKSPACE (SQLite):
 *    - Saved Founders & Custom Watchlists
 *    - Editable Research Notes
 *    - Recent Discovery Queries & Search History
 *
 * 5. SYSTEM HEALTH & TELEMETRY:
 *    - Real-time diagnostics for Crustdata, LiteLLM, Neatlogs OTLP, Entire CLI, and SQLite
 * ============================================================================
 */

export * from './types/index';

/**
 * ============================================================================
 * FOUNDER RADAR — DISCOVERY & CANDIDATE SCHEMA CONTRACTS
 * ============================================================================
 *
 * @fileoverview Core data contracts for founder discovery and intelligence.
 *
 * ### SearchRequest Schema
 * Represents structured query parameters sent to `/api/search` to discover
 * prospective founders across global ecosystems via Crustdata People Search:
 * - `query` (optional string): Freeform natural language query (e.g. "ex-Stripe founders in SF").
 * - `employer` (optional string): Target prior or current company (e.g. "Stripe", "Google", "Meta").
 * - `role` (optional string): Target executive/founder role (defaults to "Founder").
 * - `location` (optional string): Target geographic city or region (e.g. "San Francisco", "London").
 * - `country` (optional string): Target ISO or country string (e.g. "United States", "United Kingdom").
 * - `limit` (number): Number of candidate profiles per page (1 to 50, default 10).
 * - `cursor` (optional string): Upstream pagination cursor for deterministic result streaming.
 *
 * ### CandidateResult Schema (FounderProfile)
 * Represents a normalized, evidence-grounded candidate profile returned from
 * the search engine and enriched by the deterministic transition evaluator:
 * - `id` (string): Unique identifier for candidate (matches Crustdata person id).
 * - `name` (string): Full name of the professional.
 * - `headline` (optional string): Professional headline or LinkedIn summary.
 * - `current_title` (optional string): Active leadership or founder title.
 * - `current_company` (optional string): Name of active startup venture or organization.
 * - `location` (optional string): Documented geographic location.
 * - `country` (optional string): Primary country of residence/operation.
 * - `avatar_url` (optional string): Public profile photo URI where available.
 * - `current_jobs` (CareerPosition[]): Array of active positions with verifiable start dates.
 * - `past_jobs` (CareerPosition[]): Array of past employment history with start/end dates.
 * - `founder_status` (boolean): Flag indicating detected founder / co-founder status.
 * - `transition_status` ('verified' | 'unverified' | 'insufficient_evidence'):
 *     Deterministic 3-tier factual verification based on verifiable employment dates.
 * - `transition_summary` (string): Fact-grounded narrative summarizing career chronology.
 * - `target_company_match` (optional string): Matched former employer (e.g., "Stripe").
 * - `match_reasons` (string[]): Concrete evidentiary citations linking profile to query.
 * - `tags` (string[]): Domain and category tags (e.g. "Founder", "Ex-Stripe", "Verified Transition").
 * - `data_completeness` (number): Metric score (0.0 to 1.0) of profile field richness.
 * ============================================================================
 */

import { FounderProfile, CareerPosition, TransitionStatus } from './types/index';

/**
 * Request payload for founder discovery queries.
 */
export interface SearchRequest {
  query?: string;
  employer?: string;
  role?: string;
  location?: string;
  country?: string;
  limit?: number;
  cursor?: string;
}

/**
 * Normalized candidate result profile returned by discovery and search operations.
 * Alias for the core FounderProfile schema contract.
 */
export type CandidateResult = FounderProfile;

export * from './types/index';

entire session attach — Attach an existing agent session
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

entire session resume — Resume a stopped session (interactive picker, or by branch)
Resume an agent session.

With no argument, opens an interactive picker of stopped sessions across all
worktrees so you don't have to remember which branch you left work on. Picking
a session checks out its branch, restores its checkpoint session log, and asks
whether Entire should start the agent. If the branch is already checked out in
another worktree, you'll be pointed there instead.

With a branch argument, switches to that branch and resumes its session directly:
1. Checks out the specified branch
2. Finds the session ID from commits unique to this branch (not on main)
3. Restores the session log if it doesn't exist locally (an existing local log
   is kept as-is; use --force to overwrite it from the checkpoint)
4. In an interactive terminal, asks whether to start the agent; otherwise prints
   the command to resume the session

If the branch doesn't exist locally but exists on origin, you'll be prompted
to fetch it.

If newer commits without checkpoints exist on the branch (e.g., after merging main
or cherry-picking from elsewhere), this operation will reset your Git status to the
most recent commit with a checkpoint.  You'll be prompted to confirm resuming in this case.
